guide.line: Einstein held professorships in Zurich, Prague and Berlin, and in 1921 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

guide.line: On 15 January 1936, Einstein filed his Declaration of Intention — an immigrant's sworn "first papers," the formal statement that he meant to become a citizen.

guide.line: He took the oath of citizenship in 1940, keeping the Swiss citizenship he had held since young adulthood, so that he ended his life a citizen of two republics and no empire.

guide.line: He used his fame as an American deliberately: for refugees fleeing the same Europe he had escaped, for civil rights, and against the misuse of the physics he had helped create.
